bull.b: Rapid revenue growth combined with positive comparable sales and traffic indicates broad customer demand, not expansion alone. Sustained visit frequency gains can support operating leverage, reinforce brand relevance, and provide a durable base for further restaurant growth over the next several quarters.

The company is expanding while reporting strong new-unit productivity and substantial average unit volumes. This supports the economics of continued footprint growth, increases future revenue capacity, and suggests the brand can replicate its operating model across additional markets.

A debt-free current position, substantial liquidity, and positive operating and free cash flow give CAVA flexibility to fund restaurant openings and operational investments internally. This financial capacity reduces dependence on external financing while supporting execution through the planned expansion cycle.

bear.b: Profitability has improved from prior losses, but the sharp decline from the unusually strong 2024 margin shows that earnings conversion is not yet consistently durable. Lower margins leave less room to absorb cost increases and can limit cash accumulation as the store base expands.

Higher food, packaging, labor, and delivery costs are directly pressuring restaurant economics. Management expects additional increases from fuel surcharges and operational changes, so maintaining margins will require continued pricing, productivity, or sales leverage rather than relying solely on revenue growth.

bear.t: Heavy reinvestment and volatile free cash flow
bear.b: Positive current free cash flow is encouraging, but its modest conversion from net income and history of negative periods indicate substantial reinvestment requirements. Continued store development and capital spending could constrain excess cash and make cash generation more variable during expansion.
